Chapter 7: Respecting Your Body and Letting Go of Unrealistic Ideals
As you start to tune in to your emotions, you’ll find the journey leads to an even deeper challenge—learning to respect your body, just as it is, not as you think it “should” be.
In a world that’s overflowing with images of so-called “perfect” bodies, this idea might feel almost rebellious. But here’s the truth: respecting your body is at the heart of intuitive eating. It’s what makes lasting self-care possible.
So, what does it really mean to respect your body? Well, it’s not about loving every inch of yourself all the time. Instead, it’s about acknowledging your body’s needs, its limitations, and its one-of-a-kind shape.
Think about it—respect is about dignity and kindness. Sometimes, it can be as simple as choosing clothes that actually fit and feel good, instead of trying to squeeze into something uncomfortable just because of a number on a tag.
Or, maybe it’s changing the way you talk to yourself. Would you speak to a close friend the way you sometimes speak to your own body? Probably not. Offering yourself the same encouragement and respect you’d give someone you care about can make a world of difference.
Respect also means listening to your body’s signals—when it’s tired and needs rest, when it’s craving movement, or when it needs to be nourished. Instead of pushing through or ignoring those signals for the sake of chasing an unrealistic ideal, what if you honored them?
Picture your body as a trusted companion on this life journey. You wouldn’t criticize a friend for how they look or what they can’t do, right? Why not give your body that same patience and gratitude for everything it gets you through?
Now, letting go of those impossible beauty standards doesn’t happen overnight. For some, it starts with unfollowing social media accounts that only show one narrow idea of beauty. Others might seek out images and stories of all kinds of bodies, or spend some time reflecting on where their own body image beliefs came from.
Over time, your focus can shift—from how your body looks to what it can do, from picking yourself apart to appreciating your body’s abilities.
Real stories bring this to life. Maybe you know someone who used to skip swimming because they felt ashamed, but then started to rediscover the simple joy of moving in water, just for the fun of it. Or perhaps there’s someone who, after years of dieting, finally starts to notice their body’s strength and energy—no matter what size they are.
Respecting your body isn’t a one-and-done deal. It’s something you practice, again and again.
And really, that ongoing respect is the fertile ground where intuitive eating can truly grow and thrive.
